The company supplied programmers, developed systems and trained a generation of Dutch computing professionals. He built a substantial fortune through its growth and the sale of his shares, later living in Monaco as an investor.

long_biography.plain_text:
Joop van Oosterom was both a chess competitor and a patron who created opportunities for other players. A Dutch junior champion, he later won the correspondence world championship twice. His Melody Amber tournament invited leading grandmasters to compete in rapid and blindfold chess, combining two demanding forms of the game.

He also financed meetings between experienced champions and emerging players, alongside long-running support for Dutch club teams. His other sporting passion was three-cushion billiards. The Crystal Kelly tournament, named after his younger daughter, brought together leading international players. He also sponsored the Dutch league teams Crystal Kelly and Melody Amber.
